differences.message_quote: white-bear steering (WBS, Raman 2026) — which extracts a *think − don't-think* stance direction from WSB's `directed_modulation` pairs and adds it at layers 20–24 over the full prompt.
differences.what: The message gives the source's explicit citation (author/year 'Raman 2026'), its acronym 'WBS', and states it was built from WSB's directed_modulation bench pairs; the write-up only refers to it informally as 'the published white-bear (think-versus-don't-think) contrast' without naming the paper or the bench pairs it draws on.

differences.message_quote: I reconstructed that anchor through the metric server to calibrate, then developed a **new contrast of my own**
differences.what: The message describes a procedural step (reconstructing the published direction via the metric server to calibrate against it) that the write-up does not mention at all; the write-up simply reports the published direction's scores as a comparison point without describing how they were obtained.

rationale: Both documents treat Raman 2026's white-bear (think-vs-don't-think) steering as the direct prior basis the method builds on and departs from, and both make the same novelty claims (dropping the 'don't think' side, specificity to 'think about X', direction-vs-dose controls). The message is simply more explicit/detailed about the source's identity (naming the paper, acronym, and its WSB directed_modulation basis, plus a calibration step), while the write-up conveys the same credit and overlap more tersely and informally.
